label: Aristotle, Metaphysics IX.3, 1047a11-14: What is being moved toward r is able to be r: what is…
interpretation: If what is deprived of an ability is unable, what is not coming to be will be unable to come to be; and whoever says that what is unable to come to be is or will be speaks falsely, 'for this is what unable meant'. The sentence gives: what comes to be was able to come to be. Read as: what is being moved toward r is able to be r. The step from 'able to come to be r' to 'able to be r' (CanBe, DEF-CAPACITY-TO-BE) is the reading's, not Aristotle's words; it is part of the open premise STMT-WHAT-IS-BEING-MOVED-TO-R-IS-ABLE-TO-BE-R.
